Micron Technology’s vision is to change the way the world accesses information, enriching life. We show dedication to people, innovation, tenacity, collaboration, and customer focus. - Identify and implement process improvements to enhance program efficiency, governance, reporting quality, and execution effectiveness.
- Leverage digital tools, analytics, automation, and AI-enabled approaches where appropriate to improve data flow, forecasting, reporting, and support decision-making
- Partner with site and global teams to improve water performance and expand program impact
- Support compliance, audit readiness, and data assurance across relevant programs
- Present recommendations, progress updates, and arguments to executive leadership
- Drive process improvement, digitalization, and automation opportunities to enhance sustainability operations
- Coordinate external consultants, auditors, and relevant collaborators when needed

- Partner with relevant teams to evaluate project economics, validate assumptions, and support capital justification processes.

- Support executive-level decision-making by providing clear financial insights, trade-off analysis, and investment recommendations.

- Experience with Excel and data visualization tools such as Power BI or Tableau
- Familiarity with SAP, ServiceNow, or similar enterprise tools is advantageous

jobs.description:

Micron is looking for a seasoned energy procurement expert to become part of its Global Energy Procurement group. This prominent position will guide the creation and implementation of energy sourcing plans that support key semiconductor manufacturing activities across the North American region. You will negotiate and carry out sophisticated energy transactions, develop innovative commercial structures, and secure reliable, efficient, carbon-free energy solutions that contribute to Micron's long-term growth.

Working closely with executive leadership and external collaborators, you will support future manufacturing expansion through strategic energy procurement and infrastructure planning. The ideal candidate is a commercially minded negotiator who thrives in complex environments. They can balance market fundamentals, regulatory frameworks, infrastructure constraints, and business objectives to deliver creative solutions. Success in this role requires the ability to operate independently, influence senior leaders, and structure customized commercial arrangements where standard market offerings do not meet business needs.

Responsibilities

Direct negotiations for intricate energy deals, including:
- Power Purchase Agreements (PPAs)

- Virtual PPAs (VPPAs)

- Energy Supply Agreements (ESAs)

- Utility niche agreements

- Carbon-free, renewable, traditional baseload, natural gas, and LNG transactions

- Manage transactions from market evaluation through negotiation, contracting, and implementation

- Develop commercial frameworks and strategic alliances that support Micron's energy and manufacturing objectives

- Negotiate first-of-a-kind agreements involving utilities, developers, independent power producers, infrastructure providers, energy suppliers, and government partners

- Evaluate regulated and deregulated market opportunities, including utility tariffs, transmission constraints, market access programs, and infrastructure investments

- Build financial models and arguments supporting procurement decisions, portfolio optimization, investment opportunities, and risk management

- Analyze electricity trading environments, utility rate structures, fuel markets, and regulatory developments to find opportunities and reduce risk

- Lead high-level negotiations with utilities, developers, energy suppliers, regulators, and strategic partners

- Collaborate with Legal, Finance, Sustainability, Facilities, Government Affairs, and Site Leadership to advance strategic energy initiatives

- Develop executive recommendations supporting major sourcing decisions and long-term energy strategy

Minimum Qualifications

- Bachelor's degree in Finance, Economics, Business, Engineering, Energy Management, or a related field

- 7+ years of experience in energy procurement, energy origination, utility management, power marketing, energy development, commodity sourcing, or related fields

- Experience negotiating complex commercial agreements

- Solid understanding of electricity markets, utility frameworks, and energy supply agreements

- Demonstrated financial modeling and commercial analysis capabilities

- Strong communication, collaborator management, and negotiation skills

- Demonstrated ability to responsibly use AI-enabled tools to improve efficiency, analysis, market research, and decision support

Preferred Qualifications

- Experience negotiating PPAs, VPPAs, ESAs, utility tariffs, natural gas agreements, LNG contracts, or carbon-free energy transactions

- Experience supporting large industrial, semiconductor, manufacturing, or hyperscale data center energy portfolios

- Proven ability to lead complex negotiations involving energy supply, infrastructure development, utility services, generation assets, or other large-scale strategic transactions

- Knowledge of North American and APAC energy markets

- Experience with nuclear, geothermal, energy storage, hydrogen, or other emerging energy technologies

- MBA or Master's degree preferred

Why Join Micron

This is an outstanding opportunity to help build the energy strategy supporting some of the world's largest semiconductor manufacturing investments!

You will direct strategic energy sourcing initiatives throughout North America, collaborating closely with energy providers, project creators, regulators, suppliers, and executive leadership. Projects could involve nuclear energy purchasing, geothermal development, utility special contracts, LNG sourcing, renewable energy purchasing, and infrastructure solutions that support significant manufacturing growth.

The successful candidate will hold a meaningful position in securing long-term energy supply, supporting manufacturing growth, and boosting Micron's global competitiveness. You will engage with energy markets, the advancement of core systems, utility strategy, sustainability, regulatory engagement, and corporate growth while influencing billions of dollars in energy spend and investment decisions.

Qualifications
The successful candidate for this position will have:
- Excellent skills for leading or facilitating multi-organizational teams to success on complex multidimensional projects/programs
- Excellent communication skills to build teams comprised of key skills, to drive progress to plan and to get management support and buy-in for complex projects/programs
- Strong teammate to effectively collaborate with multi-functional organizations and proven track record, interpersonal, and customer service skill to comfortably work across boundaries and geographies.
- Professional, organized, meticulous, strong analytical, problem-solving, and facilitation skills. Able to independently complete tasks and adapt to constantly evolving environment.
- 5 or more years of Facilities Semiconductor industry engineering experience will be preferred
- Project/Program management experiences are preferable

jobs.description:
Our vision is to transform how the world uses information to enrich life for all .
Micron Technology is a world leader in innovating memory and storage solutions that accelerate the transformation of information into intelligence, inspiring the world to learn, communicate and advance faster than ever.

Micron’s IT organization seeks a Principal Architect to lead our AI Strategy and Emerging Systems efforts. In this strategic role, you will research, investigate, track, and evaluate innovative AI capabilities. These include generative LLMs, agentic systems, and multimodal AI. You will rapidly prototype proof-of-concepts and translate innovations into clear business opportunities supported by accurate risk controls. You will partner with AI Enablement, IT, and business teams to ensure our AI roadmap stays on the forefront while upholding Micron’s values and governance standards.

Responsibilities:
- Discover, track, and assess emerging AI capabilities and trends: (GenAI, agentic systems, multimodal, retrieval, model customization, inference optimization, governance tooling, and security patterns), translating developments into relevance for Micron’s business and technology landscape.

- Architect AI Solutions & Platforms:  Define and evolve enterprise AI architecture patterns (cloud/hybrid, data pipelines, MLOps) for large-scale generative AI and modeling workloads. Design AI system integrations (LLMs, RAG, agents) with Micron’s Microsoft 365 and cloud platforms.

- Innovate and Prototype:  Lead rapid experimentation by building AI proof-of-concepts (e.g. chatbots, predictive analytics, AI assistants). Validate feasibility, performance, and cost; recommend scale-up or pivot decisions based on results.

- Assess Value & Risk:  Identify high-impact use cases across functions (manufacturing, supply chain, R&D, etc.) and quantify business value. Simultaneously evaluate data security, IP protection, privacy, fairness, and compliance, ensuring responsible AI practices in all initiatives.

- Enable Responsible AI:  Develop standards and guardrails for model selection, prompt/data engineering, and human-in-the-loop processes. Advise on red-teaming, adversarial testing, and monitoring to mitigate AI risks.

- Communicate Insights:  Translate complex AI developments into concise briefings for executives and partners. Provide deep technical mentorship to engineering teams and mentor stakeholders on AI capabilities and limitations.

- Drive AI Strategy:  Partner with AI governance and IT leadership to update AI strategy and policies. Recommend technology partnerships and stay engaged with industry forums to keep Micron at the forefront of enterprise AI.

- Proven success delivering impact in generative AI/AI models and architecture roles, including leadership contributions across enterprise environments.

- Designing and deploying enterprise-scale generative AI/AI model platforms.

- 8+ years experience across cloud ecosystems (Azure/AWS/GCP), data engineering, and full MLOps lifecycle automation.

- Strong command of modern generative AI frameworks and tooling (PyTorch, TensorFlow, LangChain, vector databases) plus robust grounding in AI governance, security, privacy, and NIST AI RMF.

- Outstanding communicator skilled in executive-level storytelling, multi-functional influence, and quickly adopting and operationalizing emerging AI technologies.

- Experience in semiconductor or manufacturing industries (understanding of MES, OT/IT integration, IP protection).

- Hands-on coding and prototyping ability in Python or similar, with familiarity of frontend technologies (for AI UX demos).

The program manager will partner closely with Global Security, Supply Chain, Procurement, Logistics, Legal, Risk, and external logistics providers to ensure Micron maintains a scalable, auditable, and response-ready operating model for high-value shipments.  This role is specifically for program management of Micron’s logistics security in the Asia Pacific region.
Responsibilities
- Serve as a subject matter expert for high-value logistics security controls across global transportation lanes, carriers, freight forwarders, and third-party logistics providers.
- Develop, implement, and maintain a risk-based logistics security framework for high-value and high-risk shipments, considering shipment value, commodity attractiveness, route risk, geography, modality, dwell time, subcontracting, handoffs, theft history, and local recovery capability.
- Define baseline and enhanced security requirements for carriers and logistics providers, including cargo-level tracking, route compliance, approved stops, geofencing, chain of custody, tamper detection, monitoring, escalation, escorting, and recovery expectations.
- Partner with Procurement, Logistics, Global Security, Legal, and business stakeholders to embed logistics security requirements into carrier agreements, statements of work, operating procedures, and supplier performance expectations.
- Evaluate carrier, telematics, embedded tracking, smart seal, monitoring, and recovery solutions to ensure the architecture matches Micron’s security use cases and supports complex handoffs across truck, air, ocean, rail, brokered, and multimodal movements.
- Manage logistics security vendor reviews, pilots, and implementation activities, including device performance, coverage, air freight approvals, global execution constraints, integration requirements, monitoring center capabilities, and response service levels.
- Establish and oversee monitoring, escalation, and recovery workflows for high-value shipments, including alert validation, carrier and driver outreach, Micron notification, law-enforcement coordination, evidence preservation, and after-action review.
- Measure program effectiveness using outcome-based metrics such as shipment loss rate, response time, false-positive rate, missed escalation, carrier compliance, device failures, recovery performance, claims support, and security control maturity.
- Conduct carrier and lane risk assessments and recommend appropriate control overlays based on threat level, route complexity, aggregate shipment value, handoff exposure, and regional recovery capability.
- Support incident response for theft, diversion, tampering, route deviation, unauthorized stop, signal loss, seal breach, cargo separation, or other logistics security events involving Micron shipments.
- Develop and maintain logistics security policies, procedures, playbooks, standards, audit criteria, and governance materials aligned to recognized industry practices such as TAPA FSR/TSR or Micron-defined equivalents.
- Prepare executive-level briefings, risk summaries, program updates, supplier scorecards, and recommendations for senior leaders and cross-functional stakeholders.

Education
- Bachelor’s Degree in Supply Chain Management, Logistics, Security Management, Criminal Justice, Business Administration, Risk Management, Engineering, Information Systems, or a related field.
- Master’s degree or advanced professional education in supply chain, security, risk management, or business operations is a plus.
- Relevant certifications such as TAPA FSR/TSR, CPP, PSP, CTPAT, ASIS, supply chain risk, logistics, or security management certifications are preferred.

Experience
Experience developing, managing, or supporting logistics security, transportation risk, supply chain risk, cargo protection, physical security, or high-value shipment programs, with demonstrated experience in the following areas:
- High-value cargo security, logistics risk management, transportation security, carrier management, or supply chain security operations.
- Implementation or oversight of shipment security controls such as cargo-level tracking, telematics, geofencing, route management, approved stops, escorts, smart seals, tamper detection, monitoring, and incident escalation.
- Experience working with carriers, freight forwarders, 3PLs, security vendors, recovery providers, monitoring centers, or law-enforcement partners.
- Understanding of multimodal logistics operations, including truck, air, ocean, rail, cross-dock, customs, broker handoffs, final-mile movements, and other shipment separation events.
- Experience conducting route, lane, carrier, provider, or facility risk assessments and translating risk findings into practical control requirements.
- Experience managing vendor evaluations, statements of work, service-level expectations, operating procedures, supplier scorecards, and performance reviews.
- Knowledge of TAPA FSR/TSR, CTPAT, high-value cargo security practices, supply chain resilience, cargo theft trends, and incident response disciplines.
- Ability to analyze shipment risk data, carrier performance, alert activity, incident trends, and security metrics to drive continuous improvement.
- Experience coordinating cross-functionally with Procurement, Logistics, Global Security, Legal, Risk, business units, and external suppliers.
- Experience preparing executive-level communications, program recommendations, and incident summaries for senior leadership.

Soft Skills Requirements
- Ability to communicate logistics security risk in clear, business-relevant language for technical and non-technical stakeholders.
- Strong executive communication skills, including the ability to prepare concise briefings, recommendations, incident updates, and decision-ready materials.
- Ability to operate effectively in high-pressure, time-sensitive, and rapidly changing logistics or security incident environments.
- Strong analytical, problem-solving, and risk-based decision-making skills.
- Ability to build trusted partnerships with internal stakeholders, carriers, 3PLs, security providers, and external partners while maintaining clear accountability for security outcomes.
- Strong program management discipline, including the ability to manage multiple lanes, vendors, pilots, controls, and improvement initiatives simultaneously.
- Ability to balance security requirements with operational feasibility, cost, scalability, customer commitments, and business continuity needs.
- High attention to detail, sound judgment, discretion, and ability to handle confidential logistics, shipment, and security information appropriately.
